lines.trans: Chef, Elena Pavlovna just arrived here!
She is already parking near our service entrance.
From this moment a day off is declared for all cooks!
Get out of here quickly, only through the main hall!
And what about our orders on the stoves?
Go, I will calmly finish everything here myself!
I am counting to three, whoever stays will get fined!
Chef, where are all our cooks anyway?
Lyova, hide quickly, sit quietly in there!
Hi, Vitya, I decided to help you today!
How great, then change clothes and take the orders!
Yes, Chef, let's start working right away!

examples.text: Стойте! Где билет, который вам только что дали?
examples.trans: Stop! Where is the ticket that you were just given?

examples.text: Где мои заказы? Там важные гости ждут!
examples.trans: Where are my orders? Important guests are waiting out there!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Здравствуйте, молодой человек, а вы вообще кто?
examples.trans: Hello, young man, and who are you anyway?

examples.text: Шеф, а где вообще все наши повара?
examples.trans: Chef, where are all our cooks anyway?

examples.text: Подожди, Витя, а кто вообще эта женщина?
examples.trans: Wait, Vitya, and who is that woman anyway?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Спорим, что я быстрее выпью три бокала пива?
examples.trans: Bet you that I will drink three glasses of beer faster?

examples.text: Лёва, быстро спрячься, сиди там тихо!
examples.trans: Lyova, hide quickly, sit quietly in there!

examples.text: Довольно быстро же ты на это решился!
examples.trans: You made up your mind about that pretty quickly!

meanings.en: to hide oneself, to take cover
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прятаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hide (oneself)', paired with 'прятаться'.

examples.text: Вы вообще в свою комнату спрятались!
examples.trans: You hid in your own room altogether!

examples.text: Кот спрятался под кровать.
examples.trans: The cat hid under the bed.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно спрятаться.
examples.trans: I urgently need to hide.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'sit', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.text: Почему ты сидишь в углу?
examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

examples.text: Я сижу в кафе.
examples.trans: I'm sitting in a café.

examples.text: Не сидел?
examples.trans: Never been in prison?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Лёва, быстро спрячься, сиди там тихо!
examples.trans: Lyova, hide quickly, sit quietly in there!

examples.text: Он как раз тихо выходил из её номера.
examples.trans: He was just quietly walking out of her room.

examples.text: Тише, дети спят!
examples.trans: Quiet, the children are asleep!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет, Витя, мы скоро едем на стадион?
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, are we heading to the stadium soon?

examples.text: Привет, Витя, я решила тебе сегодня помочь!
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, I decided to help you today!

examples.text: Привет, папа!
examples.trans: Hi, Dad!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'decided', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Привет, Витя, я решила тебе сегодня помочь!
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, I decided to help you today!

examples.text: Довольно быстро же ты на это решился!
examples.trans: You made up your mind about that pretty quickly!

examples.text: Да, а Елена решила у нас сегодня подработать?
examples.trans: Yes, and did Elena decide to moonlight with us today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он мне бутылку виски уже полгода отдаёт.
examples.trans: He has been owing me a bottle of whiskey for half a year.

examples.text: Выиграешь ты — я дам тебе ящик виски.
examples.trans: If you win, I will give you a case of whiskey.

examples.text: А если выиграю я, ты отдашь билет!
examples.trans: And if I win, you will hand over the ticket!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Сегодня на обед будет твой любимый плов.
examples.trans: Today for lunch there will be your favorite pilaf.

examples.text: Зачем мне рыба, когда сегодня главное дерби?
examples.trans: What do I need fish for when today is the main derby?

examples.text: Мы сегодня идём с тобой на футбол!
examples.trans: You and I are going to the football match today!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Прости, дорогой, тут я бессилен помочь.
examples.trans: Sorry, my friend, here I am powerless to help.

examples.text: Привет, Витя, я решила тебе сегодня помочь!
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, I decided to help you today!

examples.text: Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вот думаю сделать его новым шеф-поваром.
examples.trans: I am thinking of making him the new head chef.

examples.text: Юрий Иванович, вот ваш билет, как я обещал.
examples.trans: Yuri Ivanovich, here is your ticket, just as I promised.

examples.text: А давай я ему отдам вот этот билет.
examples.trans: Then let me give him this ticket right here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А я о здоровье твоём постоянно пекусь.
examples.trans: And I am constantly looking out for your health.

examples.text: Здорово-то как, я просто даже не ожидал!
examples.trans: How wonderful, I simply did not even expect that!

examples.text: Вот здорово, тогда переодевайся и бери заказы!
examples.trans: How great, then change clothes and take the orders!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А как же мне тогда достать рюмку?
examples.trans: Then how am I supposed to get the shot glass?

examples.text: Тогда я пойду обратно вниз на работу.
examples.trans: Then I will go back downstairs to work.

examples.text: Я настоящий хозяин этого билета, верните мне его!
examples.trans: I am the real owner of that ticket, return it to me!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'одеваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'change clothes', paired with 'переодеться'.

examples.text: Он переодевается в форму.
examples.trans: He changes into uniform.

examples.text: А ты иди переодевайся!
examples.trans: And you, go get changed!

examples.text: Быстро переодевайся, работаем!
examples.trans: Quickly change clothes, let's get to work!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Витя, у меня для тебя есть подарок.
examples.trans: Vitya, I have a gift for you.

examples.text: Спасибо, дорогая, поздравляю нас с годовщиной!
examples.trans: Thank you, darling, happy anniversary to us!

examples.text: Как тебе это удалось? Их нет в продаже!
examples.trans: How did you manage that? They are sold out!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.text: Правда, потом она себе их и забрала.
examples.trans: True, later she took them back for herself.

examples.text: Тогда я пойду обратно вниз на работу.
examples.trans: Then I will go back downstairs to work.

examples.text: Витя, ты зачем билет у гостя забрал?
examples.trans: Vitya, why did you take the ticket from the guest?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.text: Почему же я должен быть таким добрым?
examples.trans: Why then should I be so kind to you?

examples.text: Почему я должен быть добрым?
examples.trans: Why should I be kind?

examples.text: Может быть, ты имеешь в виду Фридмана?
examples.trans: Perhaps you mean Friedman?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: А давай прямо сейчас это и проверим!
examples.trans: Let's test that right now!

examples.text: Уговор дороже денег, отдавай мне билет.
examples.trans: A deal is a deal, hand the ticket over to me.

examples.text: Нет, ничего передавать ей сейчас не надо.
examples.trans: No, there is no need to pass anything on to her right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.text: А теперь у них скоро родится ребёнок.
examples.trans: And now they are going to have a baby soon.

examples.text: Привет, Витя, мы скоро едем на стадион?
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, are we heading to the stadium soon?

examples.text: Есть, шеф, давай скорее начнём работать!
examples.trans: Yes, Chef, let's start working right away!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let us begin', paired with 'начинать'.

examples.text: Подождите, вы сначала послушайте меня...
examples.trans: Wait, listen to me first...

examples.text: У вас тут началась горячая пора скидок?
examples.trans: Has a hot season of discounts started here?

examples.text: Она вдруг ни с того ни с сего драться начала!
examples.trans: She suddenly started fighting out of nowhere!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Он в банке работает на перевозке денег.
examples.trans: He works at the bank transporting money.

examples.text: И как мне теперь работать? Душ сломался!
examples.trans: And how am I supposed to work now? The shower broke!

examples.text: Есть, шеф, давай скорее начнём работать!
examples.trans: Yes, Chef, let's start working right away!
